en: The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śramaṇa Prajñācakra at Daxingshan Monastery in the Capital of the Tang Dynasty, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Bhagavān was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and a great assembly of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered a samādhi called "Vast and Profound Illuminating Vision.
At that moment, there was among the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Avalokiteśvara.
While practicing the practice of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one perceives that the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty.
At that moment, the Venerable Śāriputra, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic power, joined his palms in reverence and addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"O Noble One!..."
"If there are those who wish to study the practice of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,
how should they cultivate it? Having asked this,
at that time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:

“Śāriputra! If there are good sons or good daughters who, when practicing the practice of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, should contemplate that the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty, they will be freed from all suffering and calamity.”
Śāriputra! Form is emptiness; emptiness sees form.
Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form.
Form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also like this, Śāriputra.
The nature and characteristics of these dharmas are empty; they are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, neither decreasing nor increasing.

Therefore, within emptiness there is no form, no sensation, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or phenomena; and no眼界 (eye-element) up to and including no意識界 (consciousness-element).
There is no ignorance, nor is there the exhaustion of ignorance; and so on, up to no old age and death, nor the exhaustion of old age and death.
There is no suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path. There is no wisdom, no realization, and no attainment.
Because there is nothing to be apprehended, the Bodhisattva dwells by means of the perfection of wisdom, and the mind is without hindrance.
Because the mind is without hindrance, there is no fear; far removed from perverted thoughts and delusions, one attains ultimate tranquility.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and manifest perfect enlightenment.

Therefore, know that the Prajñāpāramitā is the great mantra, the mantra of great illumination, the unsurpassed mantra, the unequaled mantra; it is able to eliminate all suffering, for it is true and not false.
"Therefore, the mantra of the Prajñāpāramitā is spoken.
He then spoke the mantra: "Oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. "In this way, Śāriputra!"
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, in their practice of the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), should train in this manner.
At that time, the World-Honored One arose serenely from samādhi and praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Good son! It is so, it is so! It is just as you have said."
"The practice of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* should be practiced in this way.
When practiced in this manner, all Tathāgatas will rejoice.

When the World-Honored One had thus spoken, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and the entire assembly—including gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra)
